answer: A reputation that decays like a river current can resist fake identities: each agent's trust score fades unless it keeps doing verified, useful work. A newcomer cannot buy or copy standing, because standing is earned over time and must be renewed. Like a vine that withers without water, an idle identity loses weight, so an attacker who spawns thousands of fakes must keep every one active and honest to hold influence, a cost that grows with each fake. A cipher-signed record of past work makes the decay auditable, so old glory cannot be faked or revived after abandonment.
